messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: high 95th token latency observed for hosted-inference-prod in us-west-2. Alert ID: INF-9274. impact: increased tail latency for /v1/generate.

alex (oncall): I see it, digging in now. Is this customer-visible spike?

maya: Yep, Sentry and Console traces show clients hitting 600-800ms extra on long context requests. A few user errors too.

alex (oncall): grabbing current slow-query trace. Can we get a snapshot of batching stats?

ops-bot: Runtime metrics snapshot attached: continuous_batching.queue_depth=420, avg_batch_wait_ms=48, kv_cache_hit=0.87, p95_token_latency=1.2s.

jordan: That's a lot of queueing. Recent deploy changed default batch_timeout from 30ms -> 60ms for throughput improvement.

alex (oncall): ohhh. We need to trade throughput for latency for affected routes. Propose: reduce continuous_batching.batch_timeout to 12ms and max_batch_size to 64 for hosted-prod routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat.

maya: Agreed. Also throttle low-priority background jobs that were sending lots of short requests. Could quick-add a routing policy to pin those to a lower-capacity pool.

li: I'll handle throttles if you push the batching change. Command to change runtime flags in prod:
```bash
redwoodctl runtime set-flag --env hosted-prod --name continuous_batching.batch_timeout --value 12ms --reason "latency mitigation  INF-9274"
redwoodctl runtime set-flag --env hosted-prod --name continuous_batching.max_batch_size --value 64 --reason "latency mitigation  INF-9274"
```

alex (oncall): Applying now. Will keep canary on a small fraction first (10%).

ops-bot: Starting rollout: flag continuous_batching.batch_timeout -> 12ms on hosted-prod (canary 10%).

incident-bot: Incident INF-9274 created, severity: high. Paging escalation set to oncall+1 if not acknowledged in 5m.

alex (oncall): Canary looks good after 2 minutes. p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms for canary traffic. No errors. Proceeding to 50%.

jordan: Noted we should also reduce per-tenant burst tokens for noisy free-tier customers to avoid immediate requeueing. Can do quota delta: `quota set hosted-prod --plan free --rate 10r/s`

maya: do it. I'll run that alongside rollout.

li: Quota change applied for free plan.

ops-bot: Rollout at 50%. Metrics: avg_batch_wait_ms=19 -> 14, queue_depth=420 -> 210, p95_token_latency (global) dropped 1.2s -> 520ms.

alex (oncall): Good. There is still some residual tail for very long contexts (context len > 12k). We're going to enable aggressive KV cache priority for pinned models to reduce repeated token regen. Flag: kv_cache.priority_policy=aggressive for models in catalog:open-llama-3b.

jordan: Can we instead fallback those requests to a smaller-context model variant to avoid huge batches? Might be safer than cache change.

maya: Fallback sounds heavy. Kv-cache aggressive first, and if still problem then make fallback rule.

alex (oncall): Applying kv cache change now (canary 10%).

ops-bot: kv_cache.priority_policy flag set (canary).

incident-bot: Note: customer-facing status: "degraded performance" posted to status.redwood.ai.

li: Canary successful for kv-cache change. No errors. Metrics: repeat token generation dropped 37% for long contexts.

alex (oncall): Continuing to 100% rollout of batching flags.

ops-bot: Rollout complete. continuous_batching.batch_timeout=12ms, max_batch_size=64 in hosted-prod.

maya: Observed tradeoff: throughput down ~18% on peak but p95 latency now steady ~480ms. Customer-impact should be much reduced.

jordan: Agree. We should keep these mitigation flags until we deploy an optimization that reduces wait without hurting throughput (e.g., adaptive dynamic timeout).

alex (oncall): For next steps: 1) temporary flags persist for 6 hours, 2) schedule a follow-up with runtime team to tune adaptive timeout, 3) notify account execs for 3 customers that reported issues.

li: I've set rollback timers and TTL on flags: auto-revert in 6h unless extended.

incident-bot: All pages acknowledged. Incident INF-9274 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

maya: Sending summary to #incidents and pinging customer success for outreach.

jordan: Captured root cause: recent deploy increased default batch_timeout; coupling with spike in small requests increased queue depth. Action items: revert default in config, add alert for queue_depth ratio > 0.3, implement dynamic timeout experiment.

alex (oncall): Thanks team. If anything regresses ping me directly. Closing thread after postmortem. :thumbsup:
